elements.char: Thanks to its robustness, our proxy can expectedly be applied to models of any brain area in
elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.label: text

elements.char: significant contribution to the LFP (as is likely in whole cortical column model taking into
elements.label: text

elements.char: account several pyramidal neuron populations, e.g., layer 2/3, layer 5, layer 6), the total LFP
elements.label: text

elements.char: can be approximated as a suitable linear combination of individual contributions if informa-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tion on the depth positions of the populations relative to the recording electrode is available.

elements.char: A major difference between the accurate LFP proxies using synaptic currents (sum of currents,
elements.label: text

elements.char: WS, RWS) compared to the less accurate proxy based on firing rates is that a spike is a very
elements.label: text

elements.char: local event in time, while the postsynaptic current following after a spike (as well as the contri-
elements.label: text

elements.char: bution to the LFP) lasts for many milliseconds. So an instantaneous firing rate proxy like the
elements.label: text

elements.char: ones we are considering based on firing rates cannot be expected to perform well (even with a
elements.label: text

elements.char: fixed delay). In laminar population analysis (LPA, [30]) the LFP time course was rather
elements.label: text

elements.char: assumed to be given by the measured firing rates convolved with a suitable (i.e., delayed expo-
elements.label: text

elements.char: nential) kernel, the rationale being that spikes causally drive synaptic currents which in turn
elements.label: text

elements.char: set up the LFP. The present RWS proxy is similarly constructed, effectively corresponding to a
elements.label: text

elements.char: suitable weighted sum of exponentially convolved presynaptic spike rates corresponding to
elements.label: text

elements.char: excitatory and inhibitory synaptic currents. The postsynaptic soma membrane potentials fol-
elements.label: text

elements.label: text
